1.stimulus:
The following text is from Northrop Frye's 1957 book Anatomy of Criticism.

Even in lyrics and essays the writer is to some extent a fictional hero with a fictional audience, for if the element of fictional projection disappeared completely, the writing would become direct address, or straight discursive writing, and cease to be literature.
1.text: As used in the text, what does the word "projection" most nearly mean?

choices.A: Prediction
choices.B: Estimation
choices.C: Elimination
choices.D: Presentation

2.stimulus: An ancient statue from the Huasteca region of Mexico represents a subject not seen before in artifacts from the area: a woman in an assertive stance wearing items used in a ceremonial ballgame. Archaeologist María Eugenia Maldonado notes that this image of a powerful athlete ______ the idea that women in pre-Columbian societies held only passive roles.
2.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: forgets
choices.B: predicts
choices.C: reveals
choices.D: challenges

3.stimulus: A construction foreperson reading blueprints and directing workers in accordance with them is engaging in an act of ______. Blueprints are replete with symbols, notations, and figures that are often incomprehensible to the uninitiated; the foreperson must convert all of that arcana into practical building instructions that are easily understood by anyone on the job site.
3.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: translation
choices.B: verification
choices.C: observation
choices.D: documentation

4.stimulus: Research has shown that regardless of musical training, most hearing adults recognize that the notes of the simple melody of "Baa Baa Black Sheep" are harmonious. Similarly, a study showed that even participants with no musical training could easily follow the underlying beat in the Brazilian samba song "Só Danço Samba" despite its often complex rhythms, raising the possibility that this capability was somehow ______ the participants.
4.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: instinctive for
choices.B: undertaken by
choices.C: imposed on
choices.D: unique to

5.stimulus: Along with traditional Japanese forms of woodwork and weaving, sashiko embroidery was revived during the mingei (folk art) movement of the twentieth century. Sashiko's functional origins as a mending technique and its use of motifs inspired by everyday life, such as tsuru (crane), reflect the principle that folk art should ______ its form and themes from the lives of its creators.
5.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: distinguish
choices.B: derive
choices.C: promote
choices.D: withdraw

6.stimulus: Imani Jacqueline Brown is an artist who blends scientific research, political activism, and various media in her work. In her exhibition Strike Gulf, she interrogated the impact of the oil and gas industry on southern Louisiana (where she grew up), incorporating core samples from deep seabeds off the Louisiana coast, oil well data, archival information about oil boycotts, and video she took in New Orleans. Strike Gulf thus stands as an example of Brown's multidisciplinary approach and use of diverse sources.
6.text: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It describes a project of Brown's that deviates from the typical approach that is described earlier in the text.
choices.B: It notes some challenges Brown faced in creating the specific exhibition that is discussed in the text.
choices.C: It signals a shift from a focus on Brown's artistic work in the first sentence to a focus on her work as an activist in the last sentence.
choices.D: It offers details about one of Brown's works that support the claims made in the first and last sentences.

7.stimulus: The 2024 movie Mean Girls, a remake of the 2004 cult classic, earned over $28 million during its first weekend in US theaters. One reason for its popularity is that the movie's marketing team used the internet to introduce new viewers to the original story before the remake was released. The marketers uploaded the original film divided into 23 short segments to a social media site popular with teenagers. The entire film received at least 750,000 views in one day, and 100,000 people started following the "Mean Girls" social media account.
7.text: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain the success of advertising for the Mean Girls remake
choices.B: To compare movie theaters in the United States to movie theaters in other countries
choices.C: To praise the actors who starred in the original version of Mean Girls
choices.D: To criticize the cost of making movies in the United States

8.stimulus:
The following text is adapted from William Shakespeare's 1598 play Henry IV, Part 1. King Henry is addressing several noblemen who are rumored to have been disloyal to him.

KING HENRY: My blood hath been too cold and temperate,
Unapt to stir at these indignities,
And you have found me, for accordingly
You tread upon my patience; but be sure
I will from henceforth rather be myself,
Mighty and to be fear'd, than my [disposition],
Which hath been smooth as oil, soft as young down,
And therefore lost that title of respect
Which the proud soul ne'er pays but to the proud.
8.text: Which statement best describes how King Henry presents himself in the text?

choices.A: He defends his calm disposition, which he sees as fundamental to his personality, and vows to maintain his tranquil demeanor even if it causes him to lose the respect of overly proud noblemen.
choices.B: He concedes that he has treated the noblemen with indifference, which in part explains why they have defied him, but he asserts that their disrespectful behavior is primarily driven by their excessive pride.
choices.C: He acknowledges to the noblemen that his tolerance of their conduct has undermined their respect for him, and he resolves to display his genuine nature, which is more forceful and compels deference.
choices.D: He declares that he has judged the noblemen's conduct in an impartial manner, and that despite their attempts to regain his trust through professions of submissiveness, they have irrevocably lost his respect.

9.stimulus: Maltese lithic (stone implement) assemblages from the sixth and seventh millennia BCE exhibit notable characteristics. Nearly all implements were fashioned from limestone—mostly from beach cobbles—rather than superior chert or obsidian, and the assemblages predominantly comprise flakes produced through direct percussion, with negligible representation of cores, blades, or retouched tools. The fairly rudimentary nature of Malta's lithic industry parallels contemporaneous Sardinian technologies rather than the sophisticated geometric microlith traditions documented in neighboring Sicily.
9.text: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: While not definitive evidence, the materials and methods used in the production of Maltese stone tools in the sixth and seventh millennia BCE are strongly suggestive of the exchange of lithic technology between Malta, Sardinia, and Sicily.
choices.B: The characteristics of Maltese stone tools from the sixth and seventh millennia BCE are indicative of a level of lithic technological development that, while not uniquely low, was less advanced than that observed nearby in Sicily.
choices.C: Although Malta, Sardinia, and Sicily all show evidence of lithic industry in the sixth and seventh millennia BCE, the characteristics of the stone tools in each location suggest three distinct levels of technological sophistication.
choices.D: The rudimentary stone tools of Malta and Sardinia indicate that these regions were largely isolated from the more advanced lithic traditions of Sicily during the sixth and seventh millennia BCE.

10.stimulus: It is common for freshwater lakes near or above a latitude of 45° north of the equator, like Lake Stechlin in Germany, to accumulate surface ice in winter. A study from 1980 to 2006 showed that, in general, the number of days per winter that such lakes have measurable amounts of surface ice is declining. However, a researcher claimed that some lakes have instead seen an increase in the duration of ice, citing as an example ______
10.text: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the researcher's example?

choices.A: both Lake Baikal and Oulujärvi, which had more than 100 days of ice in the winter of 2005-06.
choices.B: Lake Baikal, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than it did in the winter of 1980-81.
choices.C: both Lake Baikal and Oulujärvi, which had fewer than 195 days of ice in the winter of 1980-81.
choices.D: both Lake Kegonsa and Oulujärvi, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than they did in the winter of 1980-81.

11.stimulus: In a college course on urban affairs, a student asserts that increased traffic congestion in the 1990s in the United States was present both in very large cities such as New York City, New York, and smaller areas such as Albuquerque, New Mexico, Jacksonville, Florida, and Boise, Idaho; though those smaller areas may have been less affected by traffic congestion than very large cities, this congestion also worsened in them over time.
11.text: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the student's claim?

choices.A: In at least one of the four urban areas shown, the amount of traffic delay was less than 20 hours per commuter per year at one point between 1990 and 2000.
choices.B: While the annual number of hours of traffic delay per commuter was always lower in the Boise, Idaho, area than in the New York City, New York, area for each year between 1990 and 2000, the amount of traffic delay rose in both areas during this period.
choices.C: Even though the amount of traffic delay per commuter per year was greater in the Albuquerque, New Mexico, area than in the New York City, New York, area throughout the period from 1990 to 2000, the amounts were nearly identical in 1996.
choices.D: In 1992, the amount of traffic delay in the New York City, New York, area was less than 30 hours per commuter per year.

12.stimulus: Flatland is an 1884 novel by Edwin A. Abbott. The narrator describes the novel's setting as a world consisting entirely of two-dimensional geometric figures, whose existence is confined to the surface of a plane:
12.text: Which quotation from Flatland most effectively illustrates the claim?

choices.A: As early as the eleventh century of our era, triangular houses were universally forbidden by Law, the only exceptions being fortifications, [gun]powder magazines, barracks, and other state buildings, which it is not desirable that the general public should approach.
choices.B: Every human being in Flatland is a Regular Figure, that is to say of regular construction. By this I mean that a Woman must not only be a line, but a straight line; that an Artisan or Soldier must have two of his sides equal.
choices.C: Imagine a vast sheet of paper on which straight Lines, Triangles, Squares, Pentagons, Hexagons, and other figures, instead of remaining fixed in their places, move freely about, on or in the surface, but without the power of rising above or sinking below it...and you will then have a pretty correct notion of my country.
choices.D: The sizes of the [figures'] sides would of course depend upon the age of the individual.... A tall adult Woman might extend to a length of about eleven inches; as for the measurable quantity of the sides of a Square or Triangle, they would typically range from about ten to twelve inches.

13.stimulus: Some cosmetics contain silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs), which can leach into waterways and soils via wastewater. In a 2014 study, Merel J.C. van der Ploeg and colleagues found that Ag-NPs can accumulate in the bodies of red earthworms (Lumbricus rubellus). While bioaccumulation of manufactured nanoparticles may be inherently worrisome, it has been hypothesized that Ag-NP bioaccumulation in invertebrates like L. rubellus could serve a valuable proxy role, obviating the need for manufacturers to conduct costly and intrusive sampling of vertebrate species—such as house mice (Mus musculus), commonly used in regulatory compliance testing—for nanoparticle bioaccumulation, as environmental protection laws currently require.
13.text: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the hypothesis presented in the text?

choices.A: Given comparable levels of exposure to Ag-NPs, L. rubellus accumulates Ag-NPs at a higher rate than M. musculus does but in a fixed ratio to the rate at which M. musculus does.
choices.B: L. rubellus has been shown to accumulate several other types of manufactured nanoparticles in addition to Ag-NPs, whereas M. musculus has been shown to accumulate only Ag-NPs.
choices.C: Ag-NP concentrations in L. rubellus show no reliable correlation with Ag-NP concentrations in M. musculus when the two species are exposed to similar levels of Ag-NPs.
choices.D: Compared with M. musculus, L. rubellus can accumulate detectable Ag-NP concentrations with significantly fewer negative effects.

14.stimulus: Wayang is an art form from Java, Indonesia, that uses shadow puppets, voice actors, and music to tell stories. As long ago as the ninth century, wayang artists began to learn from and teach puppet artists from other places, including India and Persia (present-day Iran). Today, wayang performances regularly add heroes and stories from ancient Indian and Persian tales. This suggests that wayang, as it is performed today, ______
14.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: is largely unchanged from how it was performed in the ninth century.
choices.B: is more popular among the Javanese people than are other forms of storytelling.
choices.C: focuses on the specifically Indonesian aspects of the art form.
choices.D: includes elements from other cultures along with Javanese ones.

15.stimulus: Carl Woese's 1970s study of methanogens (microbes with no nuclei, such as Methanococcus vannielii, that metabolize hydrogen and carbon dioxide in oxygen-poor environments and produce methane as a by-product) suggested that they did not fit scientists' then-conventional division of life into two domains, the eukaryotes (having cells with nuclei) and the prokaryotes (missing nuclei). Molecular clock evidence indicated that what Woese argued was a third domain of life emerged as early as 3.5 billion years ago. Methanogens would have been well-adapted to conditions then given that ______
15.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: atmospheric hydrogen levels were much lower around 3.5 billion years ago than they were both earlier and later in Earth's history.
choices.B: methane, while primarily biological in origin on Earth, can be produced in the absence of biological activity.
choices.C: the earliest undisputed evidence of eukaryotes is much more recent than 3.5 billion years ago.
choices.D: Earth's oxygen levels were very low until the Great Oxidation Event approximately 2.4 billion years ago.

16.stimulus: Plants often reduce photosynthesis in undamaged parts of their leaves when other parts are being eaten by insects. It appears that feeding triggers the closure of stomata—tiny openings that allow carbon dioxide to enter the leaf—thereby limiting plants' ability to fix carbon (capture and convert it to carbohydrates during photosynthesis). In a study of genetically identical plants, those that were modified to emit an insect-deterring chemical compound experienced a smaller decline in photosynthesis under insect attack than those that did not emit the compound. Since the two types of plants showed no other differences, this finding suggests that ______
16.text: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: emitting the defensive compound enabled plants to keep their stomata open to a greater extent than they otherwise would have.
choices.B: the reduction in photosynthesis in response to insect attack is a localized rather than a systemic response.
choices.C: the insect-deterring compound itself may have a direct positive effect on the rate of photosynthesis in plant leaves.
choices.D: the decline in photosynthesis is at least partially triggered by the actual physical damage caused by insects.

17.stimulus: In 2022 Frank Condori, who studies amphibians, joined a research team for a 38-day expedition to the remote yet populous region of Alto Mayo, Peru. It had long been assumed that regions with large human ______ were unlikely to yield discoveries of new species, but team members found 27 such species, including a new species of tropical climbing salamander.
17.text: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.B: populations
choices.C: populations,
choices.D: populations, which

Begay merges geometric abstraction with realistic landscape imagery in her tapestries Palette of Cochineal (2013) and Winter in the North (2019). ______ featured alongside forty-six other tapestries of Begay's in Sublime Light, a 2025 exhibition at the National Museum of the American Indian.

23.stimulus: A young bullfrog develops in clear stages. First, it is a small tadpole that uses its tail to swim in ponds. Next, it grows into a large tadpole. Then, tiny back legs begin to appear, and after several weeks, front legs push through the skin. ______ its tail shrinks away completely as the tadpole becomes an adult frog ready for life on land.
23.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: First of all,
choices.B: Finally,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: For instance,

24.stimulus: In the past, the White House has played host to a diverse menagerie of pets, including the silkworms owned by John Quincy Adams, the nation's sixth president. ______ for the last few decades, nearly every White House pet has been a cat or dog.
24.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In fact, all but a few US presidents have kept pets during their tenure in office;
choices.B: Indeed, it's been suggested that pet ownership can bolster a president's public image;
choices.C: That said, recent US presidents have stuck to more conventional choices;
choices.D: Ultimately, Adams's uncommon pet choice had little bearing on his political legacy;

25.stimulus: Stargazers who looked up at the right time (and with the right protective equipment) on October 21, 1930, were able to enjoy the beautiful totality of a total solar eclipse. ______ Spectators had just one minute, fifty-five seconds to watch the dramatic moment when the moon almost entirely blocks the sun.
25.text: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However, this wasn't all they saw.
choices.B: The phenomenon was brief, though.
choices.C: Eventually, the event concluded as expected.
choices.D: In fact, such phenomena are fairly common.

26.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cranberry juice has a pH value of approximately 3.4.
• Grapefruit juice has a pH value of approximately 4.0.
• Substances with pH values below 7 are acidic.
26.text: The student wants to say what cranberry juice and grapefruit juice have in common. Which choice best uses information from the notes to do this?

choices.A: Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice are both acidic substances.
choices.B: Cranberry juice has a pH value that makes it acidic.
choices.C: Cranberry juice and grapefruit juice have pH values of approximately 3.4.
choices.D: Some acidic substances have pH values of approximately 4.0.

27.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In a 2021 study, researchers showed participants sets of images.
• Each set contained an unaltered image of a different character or logo alongside two slightly altered versions.
• Participants were asked to identify the correct version in each set.
• In the set containing Pikachu, 26.8% of participants selected the correct version, and 73.2% selected an altered version.
• In the set containing Scooby-Doo, 80.6% of participants identified the correct version, and 19.4% selected an altered version.
27.text: The student wants to explain how participants performed on the set with Scooby-Doo. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Pikachu and Scooby-Doo were both included in a 2021 study.
choices.B: When shown an image set of Scooby-Doo, 80.6% of participants identified the correct version, and 19.4% selected an altered version.
choices.C: In a 2021 study, researchers showed participants sets of images containing unaltered versions of popular characters or logos, such as Scooby-Doo, alongside two altered versions.
choices.D: While 80.6% of participants selected the correct version of Scooby-Doo, just 26.8% selected the correct version of Pikachu.
